## 🎯 The task

Forecast **your series from Week 4** with seasonal ARIMA, $\text{ARIMA}(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)_m$ — the *ARIMA
Models, Part 2* lecture. The order matters, and it is marked:

1. **Difference** — $D$ and $d$ from the tests, $\log y$ if the seasonal swing grows with the level.
2. **Read** the ACF and PACF of the differenced series: $p, q$ at lags $1, 2, 3$; $P, Q$ at lags
   $m, 2m, 3m$.
3. **Specify by hand** at least two candidates — then add `AutoARIMA`.
4. **Decide** on a rolling origin, check the residuals with $p + q + P + Q$, submit.

ARIMA only: no ETS, no regression, no averaging with other methods. Combining is next week's lecture.

::: {.callout-important}

::: {.callout-note}
## What the pool guarantees, and what it does not

Every series in the pool was issued only if **`AutoARIMA` with `season_length=m`, fitted on the whole raw
history**, beats its benchmark on the hidden horizon. That is a guarantee about that one model: not
about every seasonal ARIMA, not about `AutoARIMA` on $\log y$, and not about the orders `AutoARIMA` found
on `train`.

Measured on the whole pool with this template: choosing among the airline model and `AutoARIMA`, each
with and without a log, by `rolling_mase`, beats the benchmark on **89%** of series, comes within 10% on
another **9%**, and loses on **2%**. `AutoARIMA` on the raw history alone beats it on all 140 — the
screen guarantees that.

Hand-specified models and logs are what the rubric asks you to try — follow your evidence, and say in 3.2
what it was.
:::

## ✍️ Section 3 — Justification block (3 points)

The part a human reads closely. Roughly a paragraph each, with numbers from your own cells.

| Item | Points | What earns them |
|------|------:|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3.1 | 1 | **The specification, before the machine.** $D$, $d$ and the log decision, each tied to a test or a plot. The lags at the start of the ACF/PACF that named $p, q$, and the seasonal lags that named $P, Q$. |
| 3.2 | 1 | **What `AutoARIMA` chose, and what you submitted.** Where it agrees or disagrees with your reading, and why. Your candidates with AICc and rolling MASE. The model you submitted and the evidence for it — and if it is not `AutoARIMA`'s choice, what made you leave it. |
| 3.3 | 1 | **What is left, and what you expect.** Ljung-Box with $p + q + P + Q$ degrees of freedom, read. The residual autocorrelation at lag $m$, against your Lab 6 model. The interval's coverage on the validation window. Your expected skill — and if you expect to lose, why. |

::: {.callout-important}
Marked on the reasoning. A hand reading that `AutoARIMA` overrules, with a clear account of why, scores
full marks in 3.1 and 3.2. So does a model that loses to the benchmark, if 3.3 explains the loss with
numbers.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Where this goes wrong

- **Reading only the first lags.** $P$ and $Q$ live at $m, 2m, 3m$ — the shaded lags on the template's
  plot. A spike at lag 12 with nothing at 24 is a seasonal MA(1); a decay over 12, 24, 36 is seasonal AR.
- **Two seasonal differences.** $D \le 1$, always, and $d + D \le 2$.
- **Comparing AICc across different $d$, $D$ or log choices.** Across those, `rolling_mase` decides.
- **Ljung-Box with $p + q$ only.** The seasonal terms spend degrees of freedom too: $p + q + P + Q$.
- **Freezing `AutoARIMA`'s orders from `train`.** If you choose `AutoARIMA`, submit it refitted on all of
  `y` — that is the model the pool guarantee is about.
- **Forecasting from `train`.** The submission is refitted on the whole history.

📖 [FPP3 §9.9 seasonal ARIMA](https://otexts.com/fpp3/seasonal-arima.html) ·
[§9.10 ARIMA vs ETS](https://otexts.com/fpp3/arima-ets.html) ·
[FPP the Pythonic Way, ch. 9](https://otexts.com/fpppy/nbs/09-arima.html)
:::
